chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from al-Khashshab, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'An owned slave has wealth in his hands; is Zakat upon him?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No.' I said, 'And not upon his master?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No. It is what he did not give to his master, and it is not for the owned slave.'
ai.seo_question: Is Zakat due on the wealth of an owned slave in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the dual nature of the *mamluk*'s financial independence, establishing that Zakat is not levied on the slave's wealth nor on the master, as the property has not yet been transferred to the master's possession. This ruling highlights the distinct legal status of owned slaves in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing their wealth from both the master's estate and the slave's personal liability for Zakat until specific conditions of transfer or ownership are met. It underscores the principle that Zakat is tied to actual possession and control rather than mere potential ownership.
